sources.content: Spec NC-7: approval gates for the Nethercomb model registry. Nethercomb stores trained models and promotes them through three stages: staging, canary and production. Today any engineer with write access can promote a model straight to production, and in September a model with a broken tokenizer reached production this way. This spec requires a passing evaluation report before any promotion out of staging. Promotion to production also needs approval from one person on the model's owner list who did not train it.

Details. The evaluation report must come from the `nc-eval` job and be no more than 72 hours old at promotion time. Canary traffic is fixed at 5 percent, and a model must stay in canary for at least 24 hours. Emergency rollback to the previous production model skips all gates. The registry API returns HTTP 409 when a promotion is blocked, with a reason in the body. Rollout date: 2 February 2027. Out of scope: gates for models used only in offline batch scoring.

claims.text: Nethercomb promotes models through staging, canary and production.
A Nethercomb model must stay in canary for at least 48 hours.
Emergency rollback in Nethercomb skips all promotion gates.
The Nethercomb registry API returns HTTP 403 when a promotion is blocked.
Nethercomb production promotion needs approval from an owner who did not train the model.
A Nethercomb evaluation report must be no more than 72 hours old at promotion time.
